text:
sam: Quick check: proposing a small "resume window" protocol for the gateway. Emit lightweight beacons with (seq, resume_blob, emitted_bytes) every ~N tokens so gateway can try delta resumes instead of full replays.
lina: How do we keep this safe? If a resume is accepted mid-flight, client could see duplicates.
own: Plan: resume_blob is signed by runtime and includes seq+expiry. Gateway keeps last_emitted_seq and last_blob per stream, dedupes by seq on emission. If resume is accepted, runtime guarantees it will only stream tokens with seq > requested seq. Gateway drops anything <= last_emitted_seq.
sam: We also add a per-route resume_budget (tokens or attempts) so a noisy client can't cause repeated resumes. Budget resets per-request and is rate-limited per-tenant.
lina: Transport: HTTP chunk metadata for chunked responses; for gRPC a small control frame. We'll include examples in RFC.
own: For runtimes that can't sign blobs, mark model non-resumable in catalog and gateway will not emit blobs for that route.
sam: Failure modes: if resume verification fails, gateway will either hedge (start fresh request) or fast-fail based on route policy. We'll default to hedge with exponential backoff.
lina: Observability: counters: beacon_emit, resume_attempt, resume_accept, resume_reject, duplicate_drop. Also histogram resume_latency_ms.
deploy-bot: canary: resume-window feature-flag toggled on staging (gateway-canary-2025-03-03) :white_check_mark:
own: Perf sims next: try RTTs 200/500/800ms, model-chunk 300/900ms, concurrency up to 30k. Tune beacon interval and resume_budget.
sam: I'll add a short appendix to the RFC describing the budget calculation and sample wireframes. :thumbsup:
